title: Inversion of Object
statement:
Write `invertObject(obj)`. The argument `obj` is a JSON object or a JSON array whose values are all strings. Return a new object in which keys and values trade places: every distinct value of `obj` becomes a key of the result, and that key maps to the key of `obj` holding the value. When `obj` is an array, its keys are the indices written as strings (`"0"`, `"1"`, ...).

- If two or more keys of `obj` hold the same value, that value maps to an **array** of all of those keys, listed in the order of `Object.keys(obj)` (integer-like keys in ascending order first, then the other keys in their original order).
- A value held by exactly one key maps to that key as a plain string, not a one-element array.
- The result is always an object, even when `obj` is an array. The order of its keys does not matter.
constraints: obj is a JSON object or a JSON array
Every value in obj is a string
Neither a key nor a value of obj is "__proto__"
api: invertObject(obj: Record<string, string> | string[]): Record<string, string | string[]>
notes:
## Intuition

Inverting is a single pass: each entry `key -> value` of `obj` becomes `value -> key` in a new map. The only complication is a collision, when a second key holds a value already seen. The map entry for that value then has to grow from a single string into an array, and every later key with the same value is appended to it. Because `Object.keys` works the same way for arrays (it lists the indices as strings), arrays need no special case. At the end, `Object.fromEntries` turns the map into the plain object the problem returns. (The brute force instead collects, for each distinct value, every key holding it with a `filter`, which is simpler but quadratic.)

## Approach

1. Start with an empty map `inverted`.
2. Walk `Object.keys(obj)` in order and read each `value = obj[key]`.
3. If `inverted.has(value)` is false, `set` that value to `key` as a string.
4. Otherwise, if `inverted.get(value)` is already an array, push `key` onto it.
5. Otherwise (it holds one string), `set` the value to the array `[old key, key]`.
6. Return `Object.fromEntries(inverted)`, the map as a plain object.

## Example 1, step by step

`obj = { a: "1", b: "2", c: "3", d: "4" }`.

- `a` holds `"1"`, which `inverted` does not have yet, so `inverted.set("1", "a")`.
- `b`, `c` and `d` do the same with `"2"`, `"3"` and `"4"`.
- No value repeats, so the answer is `{ "1": "a", "2": "b", "3": "c", "4": "d" }`.

In Example 2, `c` meets `"2"` again, so the map entry for `"2"` changes from `"b"` to `["b", "c"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) for n entries: each key is visited once and every map update is O(1) (amortized for `push`).
- Space: O(n) for the map and the object built from it.

## Pitfalls

- Testing `if (inverted.get(value))` instead of `inverted.has(value)`: a stored key such as `""` is falsy, so its value would look unseen. A plain object would add another trap, since names like `"constructor"` look present through its prototype; a `Map` has no inherited keys.
- Always wrapping keys in arrays: a value held once must map to a plain string.
- Overwriting on a collision (`inverted.set(value, key)`) silently loses the earlier keys.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `inverted` | a map from each value of `obj` to its key or list of keys, returned as a plain object |
| `key` | the current key of `obj` (an index string for arrays) |
| `value` | the string `obj` holds at `key`, which becomes a key of `inverted` |

narration.1: invertObject builds a brand-new object instead of changing obj.
narration.2: inverted is a Map from each value of obj back to the key, or keys, holding it.
narration.3: Object.keys lists the keys in order; for an array these are the indices as strings.
narration.4: value is the string stored under key, and it becomes a key of inverted.
narration.5: has tells whether this value has been seen before; a Map has no inherited keys, so even a value like "constructor" starts out missing.
narration.6: First time this value appears: it maps to this key as a plain string.
narration.7: The value has already collected two or more keys, so it holds an array.
narration.8: Append this key so the list keeps the order of obj.
narration.10: Second time the value appears: turn the single key into an array of both keys.
narration.13: Every entry has been flipped; Object.fromEntries turns the map into the plain object the problem asks for.
